display.purpose: Hero masthead ('VINU / VARGHESE') and the 404 page's '404' digits only — double-height, scaleY(1.15).

headline.purpose: Every PageHeader page-number + title pair (200 About, 300 Work, 400 Skills, 500 Contact) — double-height, scaleY(1.15).

title.purpose: Experience role headings and the Skills active-subpage title.

label.purpose: Nav chips, stat captions, terminal chrome, contact-row labels, prompt copy.

shadows.name: terminal-detach
shadows.purpose: The terminal modal panel's only shadow, separating it from the scrim/page behind it.

shadows.name: cta-inset-groove-light
shadows.purpose: Draws a double-border groove just inside the hero primary CTA's 2px ink border (light register). Removed on hover when the button fills solid.

shadows.name: cta-inset-groove-dark
shadows.purpose: Dark-register equivalent of cta-inset-groove-light, paired with the CTA's cyan border.

motion.name: blink
motion.purpose: Terminal-style cursor blink after the hero's 'whoami' prompt.

motion.name: pour-in
motion.purpose: The system's one authored scroll-reveal: a clip-path wipe (inset 100%→0% from the left, stepped) simulating a broadcast page arriving. Applied to [data-reveal] elements via IntersectionObserver, skipped entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: skills-auto-advance
motion.value: setInterval 6000ms, cleared on HOLD or prefers-reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Auto-advances the Skills subpage carousel through categories 401-406; a genuine broadcast-subpage-cycling device, not decoration.

components.name: Primary CTA (SELECT button)
components.description: Hero's outline CTA with an inset double-border groove; the system's one inset-shadow button treatment.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-family: 'VT323', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 1.125rem; background: transparent; color: #14120f; border: 2px solid #14120f; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px #f7f5f0; padding: 10px 20px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease, box-shadow 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover, .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { background: #14120f; color: #f7f5f0; box-shadow: none; outline: none; }

components.name: Page-Address Nav Chip
components.description: Numbered page chip (100 HOME, 200 ABOUT, ...); filled blue at rest, filled cyan when active. Broadcast-colored in both light and dark register.
components.css: .ds-nav-chip { font-family: 'VT323', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 1.125rem; line-height: 1; padding: 6px 12px; border: 1px solid #12206b; background: #12206b; color: #ffffff; text-decoration: none; display: inline-block; transition: border-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-nav-chip:hover { border-color: #00ffff; } .ds-nav-chip--active { background: #00ffff; border-color: #00ffff; color: #000000; }

components.name: Alert Chip (LIVE / 404 header)
components.description: Small filled alert badge; used for the hero's LIVE tag and the 404 page's header bar.
components.css: .ds-chip-alert { font-family: 'VT323', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 1.25rem; background: #b30000; color: #ffffff; padding: 2px 8px; display: inline-block; }

components.name: Page Header (double-height)
components.description: Double-height page-number + title pair used at the top of every content section, followed by a dashed tt-rule.
components.css: .ds-page-header { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 16px; } .ds-page-header__num, .ds-page-header__title { font-family: 'VT323', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 3rem; line-height: 1; color: #14120f; transform: scaleY(1.15); transform-origin: bottom; margin: 0; } .ds-page-header__rule { margin-top: 16px; border-top: 1px dashed rgba(20,18,15,0.35); }

components.name: Experience Item (tt-frame + chrome bar)
components.description: Framed content unit with a broadcast-blue 'ITEM 30N' header bar, always white-on-blue regardless of register.
components.html:
ITEM 301Jan 2010 - Present

Technical Architect

Xminds Infotech Pvt Ltd — Trivandrum
components.css: .ds-frame { border: 2px solid #14120f; } .ds-frame__bar { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: baseline; background: #12206b; color: #ffffff; font-family: 'VT323', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 1.125rem; padding: 8px 20px; } .ds-frame__body { padding: 24px; font-family: 'VT323', ui-monospace, monospace; } .ds-frame__body h3 { font-size: 1.875rem; margin: 0; } .ds-frame__body p { color: rgba(20,18,15,0.75); margin: 4px 0 0; }

components.name: Skills Subpage Carousel
components.description: Signature component: a single tt-frame with a blue subpage-number bar (401-406) plus a HOLD/HELD toggle, auto-advancing every 6s.
components.css: .ds-carousel__bar { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: #12206b; padding: 12px 16px; } .ds-carousel__label, .ds-carousel__num, .ds-carousel__hold { font-family: 'VT323', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 1.125rem; color: #ffffff; } .ds-carousel__num { padding: 2px 10px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.4); background: transparent; cursor: pointer; } .ds-carousel__num--active { background: #00ffff; color: #000000; border-color: #00ffff; } .ds-carousel__hold { margin-left: auto; padding: 2px 10px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.4); background: transparent; cursor: pointer; }

components.name: Theme Toggle Dropdown
components.description: AUTO / PRINT / BROADCAST theme selector inside a tt-frame dropdown, in-world labels rather than generic 'system/light/dark'.
components.css: .ds-theme-menu { width: 160px; border: 2px solid #14120f; background: #f7f5f0; } .ds-theme-menu__item { display: flex; width: 100%; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 8px 16px; font-family: 'VT323', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 1.125rem; background: transparent; border: none; color: #14120f; cursor: pointer; text-align: left; } .ds-theme-menu__item:hover { background: #12206b; color: #ffffff; } .ds-theme-menu__item--active { background: #00ffff; color: #000000; }

narrative.overview:
This is a broadcast teletext service, not a scrolling resume — a CEEFAX/Ceefax-register system where content lives on numbered pages (100 Home, 200 About, 300 Work, 400 Skills, 500 Contact) and arrives like a live bulletin rather than unrolling as a webpage. The grammar is entirely broadcast-native: a rigid character grid, block-bordered content units, double-height headers, and a fixed six-color role palette (yellow/cyan/green/red/red-chip/blue) applied by function, never by decoration. One typeface — VT323 — carries every line of copy, matching the single-glyph-set character grid of real teletext hardware rather than pairing a display face against a body face.

The system runs two registers, not a simple light/dark toggle. Dark mode is the broadcast register: pure black ground, white body text, and the full role palette in play. Light mode is the printed-teletext register: body text and hairlines fall back to plain ink on paper, as if the page had been printed from the broadcast signal — but small filled chips (page-address nav pills, the LIVE tag, the 404 page header) keep their broadcast color as stamped badges on paper in both registers, per real teletext-adjacent print convention. That asymmetry is deliberate and load-bearing, not an inconsistency to fix.

Explicit anti-reference: this is not the '/01 About'-numbered engineering-blueprint identity that preceded it, and it is not a generic dark-gradient developer portfolio. No copper accent, no blueprint grid, no Space Grotesk/JetBrains Mono pairing carries forward — the only survivor from that world is the zero-border-radius invariant and a shared seriousness about engineering credibility.
keyCharacteristics: Content is addressed as numbered pages (100/200/300/400/500), keyed and clicked like a real teletext service, not scrolled as anonymous sections
One typeface (VT323) for all type, in both roles — no display/body pairing
A fixed six-color broadcast palette (yellow, cyan, green, red, red-chip, blue) applied strictly by function
Two registers: full-color broadcast (dark) vs. ink-on-paper printed (light) — with filled chips exempt from the light-mode fallback
Double-height page numbers and titles (scaleY(1.15)), a real teletext typographic convention
Depth reads through 2px solid tt-frame borders and dashed tt-rule dividers, not ambient shadows
Zero border-radius everywhere — the one invariant carried over from the prior 'Engineering Blueprint' system

rules.name: The Chip Exception Rule
rules.body: Filled chips with a solid background and white/black text — page-address nav pills, the LIVE tag, the 404 page header — keep their broadcast color in both the printed and broadcast register. Everything else (running text, hairline borders, stat/data figures) falls back to plain ink-on-paper in light mode via a dark: pairing. A color's use as a small stamped badge is what exempts it from the light-mode fallback; a color used as running text or a resting number never is.

rules.name: The Six-Role Palette Rule
rules.body: Only six functional hues exist system-wide — yellow (display), cyan (signal/active), green (data), red (alert, reserved), red-chip (alert, shipped), blue (structural chrome) — plus the register-appropriate neutral pair. No color is introduced outside these roles; a new chip or accent must be justified against this list, not invented ad hoc.

rules.name: The One Glyph Rule
rules.body: Every line of type on the site — hero name, body prose, nav chips, terminal output — renders in VT323. No second family is introduced for contrast or hierarchy; hierarchy comes entirely from size, the double-height transform, and color role.

rules.name: The Double-Height Rule
rules.body: Page numbers and titles apply transform: scaleY(1.15); transform-origin: bottom — the hero masthead, every PageHeader, and the 404 digit block. This mimics real teletext's double-height row convention and is reserved for that exact role; it does not apply to body text, labels, or card titles.

rules.name: The Bordered-Not-Shadowed Rule
rules.body: Structural depth is a border or a dashed rule, never a resting shadow. A shadow appearing on a piece of content at rest (not a modal, not an inset CTA groove) is a bug, not a variant.

dos: Do keep every corner square. Zero border-radius is a hard invariant carried over unchanged from the prior system.
Do set VT323 for all type, in every role — no second typeface, ever.
Do keep filled chips (nav pills, LIVE tag, 404 header) broadcast-colored in light mode, per the Chip Exception Rule — do not let them fall back to ink-on-paper.
Do let running text, borders, and stat/data figures fall back to plain ink in light mode via dark:-prefixed color roles.
Do use scaleY(1.15) on page numbers and titles only — the Double-Height Rule is reserved for that role.
Do use tt-frame (2px solid border) and tt-rule (1px dashed) for structural separation instead of shadows or elevation.
Do use Chip Red (#b30000) rather than bare Alert Red (#ff0000) for any small filled badge that needs reliable white-text contrast.
Do treat cyan as the system's primary interactive/active signal — active nav state, focus rings, selection, hover, primary CTA.
donts: Don't round any corner, anywhere, for any reason.
Don't pair VT323 with a second font for 'hierarchy' — hierarchy comes from size, the double-height transform, and color role only.
Don't add a resting drop-shadow to page content. The terminal's detach shadow and the hero CTA's inset groove are the only two exceptions, both named above.
Don't introduce a color outside the six-role palette (yellow/cyan/green/red/red-chip/blue) plus the two register-neutral pairs.

Don't reintroduce the prior 'Engineering Blueprint' identity — copper accent, blueprint grid texture, Space Grotesk/JetBrains Mono pairing, /01-style numbered sections. None of it carries forward except zero-radius.
Don't avoid dither/halftone rendering on the assumption it's off-brand — it's a native device of this world that the current build simply hasn't reached yet.
